result.topic_en: Euler tabulates the residues of cubes for the primes 7, 13 and 19 (of the form 3n+1), notes that each residue occurs three times, and explains this using the residue −1 of (3n)^3 and the factorisation of 1+f^3.

$19$ | $1,\ 8,\ 8,\ 7, -8,\ 7,\ 1, -1,\ 7, -7,\ 1, -1, -7,\ 8, -7, -8, -8, -1,\ 0$
vbi manifesto quoduis residuum ter occurrit; totics-
que idem signo $-$ affectum: cuius ratio inde est
perspicua, quod postremus cuiusque ordinis cubus
$(3n)^3$ pro residuo dat $-1$, et producta ex binis re-
siduis semper quoque inter residua reperiantur. Cum
igitur praeter cubum $(3n)^3$ semper dentur duo mi-
nores pariter residuum $-1$ habentes, qui sint $f^3$ et
$g^3$, erunt formulae $1+f^3$ et $1+g^3$ per $3n+1$
diuisibiles, et quia neque $1+f$ neque $1+g$ diui-
sionem admittit, necesse est vt hae $1-f+ff$ et
$1-g+gg$ sint diuisibiles; vbi quidem obseruare
licet semper esse debere $g=-ff$ vel $g=m(3n+1)-ff$
quia tum fit $1+g^3=1-f^6$, quae aeque ac $1+f^3$
est diuisibilis.

items.english: where clearly every residue occurs three times, and just as often the same residue affected with the sign minus.

items.quote:
Cum
igitur praeter cubum $(3n)^3$ semper dentur duo mi-
nores pariter residuum $-1$ habentes, qui sint $f^3$ et
$g^3$, erunt formulae $1+f^3$ et $1+g^3$ per $3n+1$
diuisibiles, et quia neque $1+f$ neque $1+g$ diui-
sionem admittit, necesse est vt hae $1-f+ff$ et
$1-g+gg$ sint diuisibiles
items.english: Since therefore, besides the cube (3n)^3, there are always two smaller cubes likewise having residue −1, call them f^3 and g^3, the formulas 1+f^3 and 1+g^3 will be divisible by 3n+1; and since neither 1+f nor 1+g admits division, it is necessary that 1−f+ff and 1−g+gg be divisible.

items.quote:
vbi quidem obseruare
licet semper esse debere $g=-ff$ vel $g=m(3n+1)-ff$
quia tum fit $1+g^3=1-f^6$, quae aeque ac $1+f^3$
est diuisibilis.
items.english: where indeed one may observe that it must always be that g = −ff, or g = m(3n+1) − ff, because then 1+g^3 = 1−f^6, which is divisible just as 1+f^3 is.
